q: Under NHA site-selection criteria, denser housing projects should generally be located on land with:
o: A single fixed slope requirement regardless of how dense the project is
The flattest terrain available, no matter what the project's density is
n: The NHA's site-selection guidelines tie the allowable slope to density: as lot/unit density per hectare rises, the maximum acceptable slope is tightened, so higher-density projects need flatter sites, per NHA Guidelines on Site Selection and Development.

q: Which space is typically located immediately next to a hotel's front desk?
n: Guests move between check-in and their rooms constantly, so the elevator lobby is planned adjacent to the front desk to keep that path short and let staff keep an eye on who is coming and going, per Time-Saver Standards for Building Types.

q: For the front row of cinema seating, what is the maximum recommended viewing angle (from eye to screen top, relative to the horizontal eye-to-screen-bottom line), per Time-Saver Standards?
n: To keep front-row viewing comfortable and avoid excessive neck strain, this vertical viewing angle is capped at 33 degrees, which in turn sets the minimum distance from screen to first row, per Time-Saver Standards for Building Types.

q: Which flooring works best in a gym's free-weights area?
n: Free weights get dropped and set down repeatedly, so the floor needs to absorb impact and resist gouging; heavy-duty rubber flooring handles this far better than tile, bare concrete, turf, or carpet, per Time-Saver Standards for Building Types.

q: Per NHA site-selection criteria, what is the maximum slope still considered developable?
n: The NHA's site-selection criteria cap the buildable slope at 15%; land steeper than this is generally excluded from housing development because of the earthworks and stability issues involved, per NHA Guidelines on Site Selection and Development.

q: What is the NHA's maximum density per hectare for a horizontal, lot-based housing project?
n: The maximum density set for horizontal, lot-based economic/socialized housing developments is 150 lots per hectare, per BP 220, Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations.

q: Which law or issuance sets minimum design standards for economic and socialized housing?
n: BP 220 lays down the minimum design and technical standards specifically for economic and socialized housing projects, distinguishing it from PD 957 (subdivision/condo buyer protection), PD 1096 (National Building Code), and RA 9514 (Fire Code), per BP 220, Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations.

q: Which gym zone should stay visible from the staff/front-desk station?
n: Heavy free-weight lifts like the squat rack carry the highest injury risk and often need a spotter, so this zone is planned within the attendants' sightline for supervision and quick assistance, per Time-Saver Standards for Building Types.

q: To minimize cut-and-fill and retaining-wall heights on sloped land, how should a building footprint's long axis be oriented?
o: At an angle across the contour lines
n: Running the long side of the building pad parallel to the contours lets the footprint follow the natural grade, minimizing how much soil has to be cut or filled and keeping retaining walls shorter than orienting the building across the slope would, per the source document.

q: What net-to-gross efficiency figure is a reasonable target for office buildings?
n: After setting aside space for cores, corridors, mechanical rooms, and other common areas, office buildings are typically planned to achieve around 85% usable (rentable) floor area against the gross floor area, per Time-Saver Standards for Building Types.

q: Which flooring suits the common areas of an elderly-care facility?
o: Any of the above work equally well
n: Vinyl flooring gives a firm, slip-resistant, cushioned surface that is easy to clean and reduces injury risk if a resident falls, better suited to elderly care than slippery glossy tile, hard bare cement, or carpet, which can catch on walkers and wheelchair wheels, per the source document.

q: What is the NHA's maximum allowed density per hectare for 3-storey low-rise residential buildings?
n: Because vertical, low-rise housing uses land more efficiently than single-storey lots, the NHA permits a higher ceiling of 252 units per hectare for 3-storey low-rise buildings, per BP 220, Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations.

q: Per NHA site-selection rules, which of these counts as a non-saleable portion of a subdivision?
n: Non-saleable areas cover the portions set aside for circulation, community facilities, parks/playgrounds, and utilities such as the sewage treatment plant (STP), which serve the whole development and are not sold off as individual lots, per BP 220, Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations.

q: Which technique(s) make a hotel corridor feel shorter than it is?
o: Breaking the run with a change in direction
Inserting small foyer alcoves at intervals
n: Long, unbroken corridors feel institutional; jogs or direction changes, patterned flooring, and small foyer nooks all break up the sightline and make the corridor read as shorter than it actually is, per Time-Saver Standards for Building Types.

q: In a convenience store, which area should stay especially visible from the cashier's counter?
n: Self-service areas such as hot food, coffee, or fountain stations are prone to spills, mess, and pilferage, so they're placed where cashiers can watch them continuously, per Time-Saver Standards for Building Types.
